label: Orindal Records
description: Friendship frontman Dan Wriggins' solo debut strips his prose-poem lyrics down to quiet drums, classical guitar, and a big melodic organ, letting a wounded, deadpan voice turn diary-plain lines into gutting little jokes. Produced by bandmate Michael Cormier, it is five songs of fragmentary memory and small-town Maine imagery delivered with total seriousness despite the title. It works as a quieter, more confessional companion to Friendship's barroom rock.
lineage: Extends the Philadelphia Friendship/Orindal circle's plainspoken, half-spoken songwriting, itself indebted to the Drag City deadpan school of Silver Jews and Smog that runs through the whole 2020s barroom-storyteller scene.

label: Oh Boy Records
description: Tre Burt's debut sets talky, literary verses over lo-fi fingerpicked guitar and rootsy production, favoring character sketches and slow-building narrative over hooks. It was independently released in 2019 before John Prine himself signed Burt to Oh Boy Records for its wider 2020 release. It plays like a front-porch reading more than a rock show, aimed at listeners who want the Prine lineage of plainspoken, half-sung storytelling.
lineage: Directly anointed by John Prine, who signed Burt to his own Oh Boy Records, tying Burt's storytelling explicitly to the Prine/Tom T. Hall deadpan tradition that feeds the modern barroom-storyteller scene.

label: Oh Boy Records
description: Burt's second album narrates a cast of invented heroes and villains with a poet's eye for detail, closer to short fiction than confession. Fuller band arrangements surround his plainspoken, slightly raspy delivery without softening it, for listeners who want storytelling folk with some groove.
lineage: Released on John Prine's Oh Boy Records, keeping Burt's storytelling tied to his mentor Prine and the plainspoken folk tradition he represents.

label: Self-released
description: A sprawling album that gathers Jesse Welles' viral topical folk songs into a full deadpan-protest record, delivered in a flat, half-amused talk-sing that turns the grimmest subjects into wry asides. Built mostly on acoustic guitar and harmonica, it sounds like a modern update of Woody Guthrie topical folk filtered through Prine's dry humor. It suits listeners who want current-events songwriting that jokes its way toward grief rather than shouting.
lineage: Sounds like a revival of the Guthrie/Prine topical-folk lineage for the social-media era, reaching listeners through viral video rather than the club circuit.
borderline_note: Some of Welles' catalog (as Welles/Jeh Sea Wells) is straight indie rock; Hells Welles specifically is the deadpan folk record that fits C2.

label: Self-released
description: Songs about aging, addiction and small-town North Carolina life, told in long, wry, half-spoken verses that turn dark memories into deadpan jokes. Unhurried heartland-rock backing with warm, fuzzy guitars keeps it plainspoken and barroom-adjacent, for fans of conversational, funny-sad songwriting.
lineage: Sounds close to the Asheville guitar tone of MJ Lenderman's circle, applied to Prine-style conversational storytelling.

label: Yep Roc
description: Jobi Riccio's debut is coming-of-age country songwriting built on pedal steel, fiddle, and small full-band arrangements, moving from tender acoustic ballads to fuller alt-country arrangements without losing its intimate, diaristic voice. Songs about self-love, loneliness, and growing up in your twenties are sung plainly, without Nashville gloss. It suits listeners who want 2020s indie-scene country that still plays like a singer-songwriter record.
lineage: Sounds of a piece with 2020s indie-Americana peers who bring 2010s indie-folk intimacy into recognizably country arrangements.

label: Propeller Sound Recordings
description: Chapel Hill songwriter and literature professor Florence Dore blends classic-rock hooks, Americana twang and 1980s college-radio jangle. Narrative-heavy lyrics and a lived-in, veteran band sound keep it far from Nashville polish. It is built for listeners who want literate, well-crafted country-rock steeped in the history of the genre's indie wing.
lineage: Sounds steeped in the 1980s-'90s college-rock and No Depression alt-country lineage that C3 grew from.

label: Rounder Records
description: Ruston Kelly's debut is the sound he calls 'dirt emo': confessional, downcast lyrics about addiction and heartbreak set over pedal steel and plainspoken country-rock arrangements, closer in mood to emo than to Music Row polish. It moves between hushed acoustic laments and fuller, rootsy full-band tracks without losing its diary-like intimacy. It is a gateway record for listeners coming to alt-country from indie/emo rather than from classic country.
lineage: Draws on Nashville's neo-traditional and outlaw country vocabulary but bends it toward emo's confessional mode, a hybrid Kelly himself named 'dirt emo' and one that seems to echo across later indie-adjacent country songwriting.
borderline_note: Kelly's sound leans closer to pop/emo confessional than straight honky-tonk; included as a documented indie-to-country crossover ('dirt emo') rather than a core traditional-country record.

label: Nameless Knight Records
description: John Prine's son makes an unhurried, plainspoken singer-songwriter record about grief and inheritance, built on fingerpicked acoustic guitar and a warm, understated voice that avoids leaning on his father's shadow. Songs like the title track work through loss directly rather than cleverly, closer to quiet country-folk than to barroom wit. It gives the C3 scene a straight-line link back to the '70s country-folk storytellers by blood as well as sound.
lineage: The most literal lineage in the atlas: son of John Prine, carrying the plainspoken country-folk storytelling tradition (V25) directly into the 2020s indie-country scene.

label: Lightning Rod Records
description: Jesse Daniel plays it straight: shuffling honky-tonk rhythms, crying pedal steel and a plain, traditionalist voice on songs about recovery, the road and old-school country. Coming out of California punk rather than a Nashville pipeline, Daniel's traditionalism is a chosen, DIY revival rather than an inherited style. It is a straightforward entry point for listeners who want honky-tonk played by someone raised on punk rock.
lineage: A cowpunk-to-honky-tonk arc in miniature: Daniel's background in California punk bands leads into a self-consciously traditionalist sound that recalls Bakersfield, released through the independent, Nashville-based Lightning Rod Records.
